We need to produce a test class for NumericIndicator.dividedBy(Indicator<Num>) method. Use JUnit 5 and Mockito. Need to initialize dependencies: a BarSeries, ClosePriceIndicator, EMAIndicator etc. But we can reuse similar to existing tests. We'll create tests for static (Number) and dynamic (Indicator) division. But focal method is dividedBy(Indicator<Num>) which returns an Indicator (probably NumericIndicator.of(BinaryOperation.quotient(this, other))). We need to test that division works correctly.

We can create a NumericIndicator from a ClosePriceIndicator (cp). Use a constant indicator for divisor, and an EMAIndicator for dynamic divisor.

We need to assert values using assertNumEquals custom method? In this template we only have JUnit assertions. We can use assertEquals with Num objects but need equality. In the existing test they use assertNumEquals from TestUtils. We can import that static method.

Add imports: org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.ClosePriceIndicator; org.ta4j.core.indicators.helpers.VolumeIndicator; etc. But minimal: BarSeries, MockBarSeries, NumericIndicator, EMAIndicator, ClosePriceIndicator, Num, Function.

We need numFunction: In existing test they have a constructor taking Function<Number, Num>. In this new test class we can use a static numFunction from TestUtils? Not available. We can use a simple lambda: n -> new org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum(n.doubleValue())? Actually Ta4j provides DecimalNum class. But we can use org.ta4j.core.num.Num; there is a static method: org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum.valueOf(double). But we can just use series.getBar(0).getClosePrice()? Not needed.

Simpler: Use MockBarSeries with a lambda that returns DecimalNum.valueOf. In existing tests they have a field numFunction from AbstractIndicatorTest. Since we are not extending that, we can create a BarSeries using MockBarSeries(numFunction,...). Need to import org.ta4j.core.mocks.MockBarSeries and DecimalNum.

We'll set up static fields: BarSeries series; ClosePriceIndicator cp; EMAIndicator ema; Function<Number, Num> numFunction = n -> org.ta4j.core.num.DecimalNum.valueOf(n.doubleValue());

In @BeforeAll we can initialize series, cp, ema.

Test methods:

@Test void dividedByNumber() { NumericIndicator numeric = NumericIndicator.of(cp); NumericIndicator result = numeric.dividedBy(5); assertNumEquals(cp.getValue(0).dividedBy(DecimalNum.valueOf(5)), result.getValue(0)); }

But there is a method dividedBy(Number n) which internally creates constant indicator. Not needed; we test dividedBy(Indicator) directly: NumericIndicator result = numeric.dividedBy(DecimalNum.valueOf(5) constant indicator). But we can use ConstantIndicator: new ConstantIndicator<>(series, DecimalNum.valueOf(5)). Or use NumericIndicator.of(ConstantIndicator). Simpler: Use NumericIndicator.of(cp).dividedBy(NumericIndicator.of(new ConstantIndicator<>(series, DecimalNum.valueOf(5))))? Actually dividedBy expects Indicator<Num>. So we can pass new ConstantIndicator<>(series, DecimalNum.valueOf(5)). We'll import ConstantIndicator.

Test dynamic: NumericIndicator result = numeric.dividedBy(ema); assert equals cp.getValue(i).dividedBy(ema.getValue(i)).

Also test that delegate type is correct: result.delegate().getClass() maybe? Not needed.

Implement teardown empty.

Add import static org.ta4j.core.TestUtils.assertNumEquals; (assuming same utility). If not, we can use assertEquals with .equals.

We'll write code.
